body_markdown:
## Executive summary

This report examines AI document intake for small accounting firms from 5 angles using 11 sources. In this fictional survey of 120 small accounting firms, 38 percent said they already use some form of automated document intake, mostly for bank statements and receipts [1]. Adoption tends to start with one workflow, usually client document collection during tax season, before spreading to bookkeeping [2]. Client adoption of a new upload portal was the slowest part of the fictional rollouts studied [3].

## Findings

### 1. What does adoption look like today for AI document intake for small accounting firms?

- In this fictional survey of 120 small accounting firms, 38 percent said they already use some form of automated document intake, mostly for bank statements and receipts [1].
- Adoption tends to start with one workflow, usually client document collection during tax season, before spreading to bookkeeping [2].
- Client adoption of a new upload portal was the slowest part of the fictional rollouts studied [3].

### 2. What are the typical costs and pricing models for AI document intake for small accounting firms?

- Fictional vendors in this comparison charge either per seat, typically 30 to 60 dollars per user per month, or per document processed [4].
- Subscription fees are usually the smaller cost [5].

### 3. What measurable benefits are reported for AI document intake for small accounting firms?

- The fictional firm reported cutting manual data entry on client uploads by roughly half and answering client status questions faster [6].
- Field-level extraction accuracy in this fictional benchmark ranged from 85 to 97 percent depending on document quality [7].

### 4. What are the main risks, including privacy and compliance, of AI document intake for small accounting firms?

- Before uploading client tax documents to any cloud tool, confirm where data is stored, whether it is used to train models, how long it is retained, and that a written information security plan covers the new system [8].
- This fictional insurer note warns that responsibility for errors stays with the firm [9].

### 5. How long does implementation take and what does it require for AI document intake for small accounting firms?

- A typical small-firm rollout in this fictional guide takes six to ten weeks: two weeks to choose a tool, two to four weeks to configure templates and the client portal, and a pilot with a handful of clients before tax season [10].
- The main technical requirement is a working integration with the firm's existing practice management and tax software [11].
